messages.subject: Addding prior mean
parts:
Hello,

Suppose that I have a model like
formula = y ~ f(x, model="generic", Cmatrix = Q)  - 1
Can I specify a prior mean (\mu) for the first x (or any index of x's)? 
So that the latent density is \exp( - 1/2  (x)^T (\tau Q)  (x)  -  \tau_{\mu} /2 (x[1] - \mu)^2)
where I only estimate \tau.

mvh
Jonas Wallin

> Hello,
>
>
> Suppose that I have a model like
> formula = y ~ f(x, model="generic", Cmatrix = Q) - 1
> Can I specify a prior mean (\mu) for the first x (or any index of
> x's)?
> So that the latent density is \exp( - 1/2 (x)^T (\tau Q) (x)
> - \tau_{\mu} /2 (x[1] - \mu)^2)
> where I only estimate \tau.
>
>
> mvh
> Jonas Wallin

there is something called 'offset()' which are constants, which could
be added to the linear predictor, like

y ~ 1 + offset(a) + f(i)


you can have as many offset's as you like, but I don't think this is
what you want to use.

This density:

can be achived by adding a Gaussian likelihood with fixed precision
\tau_{\mu} and only observation, y[1] = \mu.
